summary: UCP natively covers agent identity (profile plus keys), expiry, key and token revocation, replay protection through idempotency keys, and monitoring signals. Consent, step-up, payee scoping, evidence and disputes are partial and depend on optional extensions (AP2, authentication) or on the business and PSP. Spending caps and reputation are absent. A controls layer acts best at the platform before complete, at the trusted review screen, and at the business edge where profiles are fetched.

native.note: Platform profile URL in UCP-Agent with RFC 9421 signatures against its keys, or API key, OAuth or mTLS bound to that profile.
Permissionless by design; businesses should keep a registry of pre-approved platforms. No know-your-agent registry.
Buyer places the order in a trusted UI unless AP2 is active; buyer_consent map; AP2 checkout_mandate as signed consent.
No cap field; limits live in AP2 mandates, the credential provider or the platform.
Tokens are handler-specific and some (Adyen) are bound to session and merchant; AP2 mandates bind the merchant-signed checkout.
Checkout expires_at defaults to 6 hours; mandate_expired in the AP2 extension.
Remove keys from the profile; RFC 7009 token revocation required for identity linking; OpenID RISC recommended.
requires_escalation handoff through continue_url; 3DS2 device data collection and challenge actions in the optional authentication extension.
Signed Idempotency-Key with 128-bit entropy, 24 to 48 hour storage and 409 on mismatch; Web Bot Auth shape adds nonce.
Order with permalink_url and a required confirmation email; AP2 mandates kept as JCS-canonical evidence.
Order adjustments can record disputes, refunds and returns; dispute handling stays with the business and PSP.
No reputation mechanism for platforms or businesses.
signals such as dev.ucp.buyer_ip and dev.ucp.user_agent, plus signed order webhooks.
Businesses can refuse platforms, answer 503 or cancel sessions; no protocol-level global stop.

gaps.title: No spending limits
gaps.description: Nothing in the checkout schema caps what an agent may buy; limits must come from AP2 mandates, the wallet or the platform.

gaps.title: Identity is not trust
gaps.description: Signatures and authority binding prove who a platform or schema author is, not that it behaves well, and there is no reputation layer.

gaps.title: Consent evidence is optional
gaps.description: Without AP2 the only consent record is the platform's trusted UI and the business confirmation email; live AP2 use is unverified.

gaps.title: Permissionless onboarding
gaps.description: Any platform with a profile can call any business, so each business must build its own allowlists and discovery budgets.

gaps.title: Disputes outside the protocol
gaps.description: Adjustments can record a dispute, but chargeback rules and liability stay with card networks and PSPs.

controlPoints.what: Decide whether the agent may buy from this business at all.
controlPoints.how: Allowlist businesses and capability namespaces at the platform; check the intersection and the advertised handlers before create.

controlPoints.what: Bind consent to the exact checkout.
controlPoints.how: Show the latest checkout in a trusted UI immediately before complete, or negotiate the AP2 extension so the checkout mandate covers the merchant-signed checkout.
Verify signatures, enforce pre-approved platform registries, cache and rate-limit profile fetches, and apply SSRF guards at the business edge.
PSP fraud screening and 3DS2 through the authentication extension's actions.
Verify signed order webhooks, reconcile with GET /orders/{id}, and track adjustments.

checklist.item: Pin schema URLs to the release tag you target, not main.
checklist.why: main carries drafts that are in no release.

checklist.item: Bind every authenticated principal to the profile named in UCP-Agent.
checklist.why: The header alone is not authentication.

checklist.item: Store idempotency keys for 48 hours and fail closed when storage is down.
Implement the lost complete response rules exactly.
checklist.why: A new key on retry can place a second order.

checklist.item: Reject profile URLs on special-use IP ranges and never follow redirects.
Remove compromised keys from keys immediately and keep cache lifetimes short.
checklist.why: A key stays valid until it is absent.

checklist.item: Verify webhook signatures and the signer's match with the order business.
Set spending limits outside UCP for unattended agents.
checklist.why: The protocol has no cap field.
